vulnerability.name: CVE-2025-15467
vulnerability.description: OpenSSL stack buffer overflow in CMS AuthEnvelopedData parsing

statements.impact_statement: This application does not parse CMS, PKCS#7, or S/MIME messages. It only uses PEM-format private keys for JWT signing and makes outbound HTTPS connections.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2025-69419
vulnerability.description: OpenSSL out-of-bounds write in PKCS#12 processing

statements.impact_statement: This application does not process PKCS#12 files. Private keys are loaded in PEM format only.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-32597
vulnerability.description: pyjwt: PyJWT accepts unknown `crit` header extensions (RFC 7515 §4.1.11 MUST violation)

statements.impact_statement: The application does not accept untrusted cryptographic input, and the JWTs it processes are signed using its own private keys for authentication with the GitHub API. Since the crit header vulnerability requires an adversary to supply a maliciously crafted JWT, and the application does not process JWTs from untrusted sources, the vulnerability is not exploitable in this context.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-44431
vulnerability.description: urllib3: Sensitive headers forwarded across origins in proxied low-level redirects

statements.impact_statement: The application only makes outbound HTTPS connections to the GitHub API using high-level APIs and does not use the low-level `ProxyManager.connection_from_url().urlopen()` method for cross-origin redirects. Therefore, the vulnerable code path is not executed in the context of this application.
